## Triage: p2 · `domain:ui` · `pm:queue` · per-string reading · triage seat · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-18T12:00Z

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015). ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

**Grade p2.** It is a ruled follow-up of objectstack-ai/cloud#3002 ruling A (`6248811507`), and the floor for a ruled follow-up is p2. The lane is `domain:ui`.

**The per-string reading the card asks for.** The rule applied: a user-facing string never names the running system by the cloud noun. A platform-internal name in code (`allowEnvironmentOverlay`, "environment scope") is not user-facing copy and is untouched. Read on objectui `origin/main`:

| key | sense | reading |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `engine.packages.description` | the system the user is in | rewrite: "installed in this system" / 「本系统中安装的」 |
| `engine.packages.noCapability` | the system the user is in | rewrite |
| `engine.packages.detail.adoptConfirm` | the system the user is in | rewrite |
| `perm.badge.custom` | "made here, not from a package" | zh 「本环境自定义」 → 「自定义」, matching en `'Custom'` |
| the four permission-set clone / lock strings ("authored in this environment") | "made here, not from a package" | rewrite: "authored in this system" / 「本系统中创作的」. The overlay is explained by "a packaged item" and "the package-provided base", which stay |

- Where an en string names the mechanism ("an environment-scope edit would overlay a packaged item"), it may keep "environment-scope" as the platform's term, or say "an edit here would overlay a packaged item". The dev picks one wording and uses it in all four strings.
- **Not this card:** `marketplace.*` (install-target copy), and `cloudWorkspaceTimezoneNotice.seeded` on the cloud home, which is a cloud surface where the cloud noun is the right one. Both are listed on the card for completeness only.
- `check:i18n-designer-parity` stays green: en and zh move together.
